key_insight: Physics-informed circuits, compact gauge-field digitization, and operator truncation advance quantum simulation of interacting-field dynamics toward QCD-relevant problems.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets limited qubit counts and circuit depths while preserving observables needed to study energy loss, hadronization, and low-energy field behavior.
method: Prepare interacting ground states and simulate a heavy quark traversing light quarks in 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory.
Digitize a fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis using as few as three qubits per plaquette.
Apply Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) to reduce operator contributions and circuit depth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware validation against classical benchmarks, low-energy observables reproduced to 10^-3 precision with three qubits per plaquette, and approximately 30% circuit-depth reduction for λφ⁴ ground-state preparation.
watch_item: Resource overhead still limits larger systems, and efficiency across all gauge couplings is expected rather than established in the abstract.
paper_title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
